newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: CRICKET-SRI LANKA, PAKISTAN MILKED OF VENOM.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-SRI LANKA, PAKISTAN MILKED OF VENOM.

text.p: Pakistan and Sri Lanka have been milked of their venom, leaving the door open for a new brigade of bowlers to make a name for themselves in the deciding second test starting in Colombo on Saturday.

Off-spinner Muthiah Muralitharan, Sri Lanka's leading wicket-taker with 107 wickets in 28 tests, has been ruled out due to a strained muscle near his rib-cage, giving Ruwan Kalpage the opportunity to emerge from the shadows of his compatriot.
And Pakistan will again have to cope without the world's most lethal opening bowling combination of Wasim Akram and Waqar Younis, who missed the first drawn test due to injury.
Akram is nursing an injured bowling arm, a result of excessive cricket, and Waqar has a fractured toe which has ruled him out of the tour.
Sri Lanka's Kalpage has played only eight tests since making his debut against India four years ago in Colombo.
Kalpage, 27, is an all-rounder who bats left-handed and bowls right-arm off-breaks.
With Kumara Dharmasena also certain to be left out, Sri Lanka will have a new spin combination of Kalpage and left-arm leg-spinner Jayantha Silva.
Sri Lanka have made a third bowling change by bringing in left-arm fast-medium bowler Sajeeva de Silva to partner left-armer Chaminda Vaas.
Nuwan Zoysa, who shared the new ball with Vaas in the first test, has been sidelined with a leg injury.
Pakistan are expected to draft in 20-year-old fast-medium bowler Abdul Razzaq, one of the replacements for Waqar and Wasim.

Razzaq, whose previous experience at international level is limited to two one-day internationals against Zimbabwe, is likely to come into the side at the expense of either fast bowler Shahid Nazir or opening batsman Salim Elahi.

Sri Lanka (from) - Arjuna Ranatunga (captain), Sanath Jayasuriya, Russell Arnold, Marvan Atapattu, Aravinda de Silva, Hashan Tillekeratne, Romesh Kaluwitharana, Chaminda Vaas, Sajeeva de Silva, Ruwan Kalpage, Jayantha Silva, Kumara Dharmasena, Sanjeeva Ranatunga, Dulip Liyanage.

Pakistan (from) - Rameez Raja (captain), Salim Elahi, Ijaz Ahmed, Salim Malik, Inzamam-ul-Haq, Asif Mujtaba, Moin Khan, Saqlain Mushtaq, Mushtaq Ahmed, Mohammad Zahid, Shahid Nazir, Abdul Razzaq, Mohammad Wasim.
